reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 3 close: SPX 7,568.92, -3.51% from its 120-day high, -1.61% below its 50-day but +3.46% above its 200-day; SMH $518.52, -22.82% from its high and between zones, just below its 200-day; NVDA $206.69 sits in Zone 1; VIX 20.83 has not rolled over and HY OAS 3.40 is calm, with the mechanical capitulation tally at 2 of 4. The Nov 4 midday bounce (SPY +1.72%, VIX down to 16.93) is intraday and unconfirmed at the close. Episode data is fresh, not stale.
reaction.invalidation: Watch is wrong in either direction: a verified bottom (tally 4 of 4 with a Zone 2 print, or two closes above the 7,750-7,820 failure zone) means Watch was too cautious and the stance should have moved to Add; a credit break (HY OAS above 4%) or SPX closing below its 200-day (7,315.89) means Watch was too complacent and the stance should have moved to Trim/Exit. Either print voids this ladder.

ladder.response: Prepare Tranche A only: require the tally to reach at least 3 of 4 (volume climax plus VIX rollover) before any deployment — a zone print alone is not a buy.
Treat as the trap case confirmed: no chasing, hold cash, expect a second low; the retest verdict decides the next entry, not the rally.
ladder.trigger: SPX rallies into the failure zone (7,750-7,820) or SMH into 580-600 and fails to hold

ladder.response: Stand down: all deployment triggers void, reassess the regime — the correction has become a regime break.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4%, VIX closes above 25, or SPX closes below its 200-day (7,315.89)

ladder.response: Re-entry confirmed: the episode is over (first case) or the bottom is verified (second case) — stance moves from Watch to Add on the pre-committed plan.

reaction.trapRisk: The midday bounce is the pivot-and-fail setup in real time: SPY +1.72% and VIX down 18.72% intraday, while SMH is still 9.19% below its 50-day and the tally sits at 2 of 4 with no volume climax and no VIX rollover. Entries change accordingly: no chasing the first bounce, no sizing on an intraday print — wait for the close and the failure-zone retest verdict, and treat any rally into 7,750-7,820 (SPX) or 580-600 (SMH) that fails to hold as confirmation of the trap, not a buying opportunity.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the benign read only while credit stays loose. The divergence itself is real — the index's calm is carried by non-Mag 7 breadth — so if HY OAS pushes toward 4% or lending standards tighten, the same tape reprices as a rollover. The rotation thesis needs credit to stay quiet.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY is only 1.8% below its 52-week high and down 1.51% over the past month, while the Mag 7 average sits 13.5% below its highs — an 11.7-point divergence gap, with AAPL the strongest at -0.4% and GOOGL the weakest at -28.9%. QQQ is down 8.76% over the month against SPY's -1.51%. Credit is not confirming a rollover: lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.40, calm.
themes.label: Index rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a leadership rotation: the broad index is holding up while the names that carried it are being sold.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or SLOOS moving out of the LOOSE zone.

themes.counterRead: A bounce that stops inside the failure zone and fails is the trap case, not the bottom. The bounce's breadth (IWM +1.46% alongside SPY) is genuine, but no entry is justified until the close confirms it or the failure-zone retest delivers a verdict — chasing the first bounce is how the correction takes the second leg.
themes.dataAnchor: The bounce is intraday and unconfirmed at the close. The failure zone sits above: SPX 7,750-7,820 and SMH 580-600.
themes.label: Midday bounce into the failure zone

themes.watchFor: SPX close into 7,750-7,820 and whether it holds for a second session.

themes.counterRead: Policy risk is real, not just sentiment: an election outcome that changes merchant-power economics can re-rate these names for longer than a day, and the KeyBanc downgrade shows the Street is already moving. But the move is priced as if the power-demand thesis itself broke, while the revenue and cash-flow data say the demand is intact — that gap is the opportunity, provided the policy read clarifies rather than worsens.
themes.dataAnchor: The selling is broad and indiscriminate: VST -14.93% today and -26.02% over the month, GEV -10.52% today, PWR -12.79% today, ETN -9.78% today, CCJ -23.73% over the month, SMR -35.97%, OKLO -42.64%. The fundamentals did not move with the price: VST revenue is growing 19.1% YoY with a 2.3x price-to-sales ratio and $1,318M of free cash flow, insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, and ETN revenue is growing 22.2% YoY with recovery confirmed. VST's RSI is 31.6, ETN's 36.9 — oversold, not broken.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power repriced by the election
themes.narrative: The midterm outcome is being read as a hit to merchant power generators: VST plunged 13.5-14% with a KeyBanc downgrade, Constellation Energy sank 8%, and the whole nuclear/power complex sold off on the result.
themes.watchFor: A second consecutive 5%+ down day in VST/CEG would confirm the election repricing is a trend, not a one-day shock; stabilization while revenue data holds would confirm the dislocation.

themes.counterRead: Multiple compression is the real risk, not the growth story: AMAT, PLTR and KLAC are flagged MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION, and SMH is still 9.19% below its 50-day with the tally at 2 of 4. Growth can keep printing while the multiple keeps shrinking, so the dislocation is an opportunity only at zone prices with tally confirmation — not a reason to buy the first oversold RSI print.

DDOG is 37.6% below its high with revenue +27.7% YoY, an 80% gross margin and a 29.2% FCF margin (score 84). LRCX revenue is up 131.3% YoY while the stock sits 49.7% below its high. themes.label: AI semis and software: growth intact, price down a third or more
themes.narrative: The market is treating the AI complex as a busted trade: NVDA -15.09% over the month, AVGO -13.17%, GOOGL -16.41%, META -14.87%, and the dislocation list runs to 35 names, most flagged sentiment-driven.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with the capitulation tally reaching 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: Calm credit is what keeps the episode a correction rather than a regime break — but it is also what makes the equity drawdown a pure repricing, with no forced-selling floor. If the Dec FOMC signals more hikes, the 10-year retests 5.2% and the credit calm is the first thing to break.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.40 and calm, well below the 4% stand-down line. The 10-year is 4.91%, below the 5.2% falsifier line, with the 2-year at 4.59% and the curve at +0.32 (not inverted); the real 10-year is 2.61% and breakeven inflation 2.30%. The Fed funds rate is 3.88%. The next catalyst is the Dec 8-9 FOMC decision, flagged HIGH signal strength and anticipated.
themes.label: Credit and rates calm under the equity drawdown
themes.narrative: Rates are the quiet leg of the tape: no credit event is forcing the equity correction, and the bond market is not pricing a funding break.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4%, or the 10-year closing above 5.2% into the Dec 8-9 FOMC.
